## Overview

`manager` provides a standardized workflow for environmental data analysis in R.

The package centers around the `env_schema` class, a standardized
environmental data model built on top of tidy data principles. Once data
have been converted to `env_schema`, they can be analyzed, summarized,
visualized, and reported using a consistent workflow.

Key features include:

- Standardized environmental data structure (`env_schema`)
- Native compatibility with dplyr and the tidyverse
- Time-series, boxplot, Piper, and spatial visualizations
- Summary statistics and reporting utilities
- Importers for MANAGES and gINT databases

## Why manager? 
Environmental datasets are often distributed across spreadsheets, laboratory 
reports, groundwater databases, and regulatory exports. `manager` provides 
a common data model(`env_schema`) that allows the same analysis and plotting 
tools to work across data sources without rewriting workflows for each project.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github("jentjr/manager")
```

## Quick Start

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(manager)

data(gw)

gw %>%
  filter(location_id == "MW-1",
         .analyte == "Chloride") %>%
  summary_stats()
```

## Environmental Data Standard

Datasets in `manager` use the `env_schema` class:

```r
gw
```

Output:

```
12345 rows × 15 columns
Locations: 48
Analytes: 72
Date range: 2015-01-01 to 2024-12-31
Class: env_schema
```

Core environmental variables include:

- location
- analyte
- result
- date

Additional metadata such as units, qualifiers, detection limits,
coordinates, sample identifiers, and analytical methods can also be
stored and preserved by the schema.

## Import Data
```{r, eval=FALSE}
gw <- read_manages3("Site.mdb")

gw <- read_manages4(
  server = "MY_MANAGES_SERVER",
  database = "MY_MANAGES_DATABASE",
  site = "MY_SITE"
)
```

## Visualize Data
```{r, time-series, fig.height=6, fig.width=9, results='hide', warning=FALSE}
# load example data and plot time series of selected wells and constituents
data("gw")

wells <- c("MW-1", "MW-2")

params <- c("Magnesium, dissolved", 
            "Sodium, dissolved", 
            "Chloride, total", 
            "Sulfate, total", 
            "Potassium, dissolved")

gw %>%
  filter(location %in% wells, analyte %in% params) %>%
  series_plot(facet_var = "param_name", group_var = "location_id")
```

```{r boxplots, fig.height=6, fig.width=9, results='hide'}
# create boxplots filled by gradient
gw %>%
  filter(analyte == "Chloride, total", 
         location %in% c("MW-1", "MW-2", "MW-3", "MW-4", "MW-5", "MW-6", "MW-7", "MW-8")) %>%
  mutate(gradient = if_else(location %in% wells, "upgradient", "downgradient")) %>% 
  boxplot(fill = "gradient")
```

Piper Diagrams and more...
```{r, piper-plot, fig.height=6, fig.width=9, results='hide', warning=FALSE}
gw %>%
  piper_plot()
```

## Interactive Exploration

manager also includes a Shiny application:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
manager::manager()
```
